literal: To those who have fear, there is no fortress; likewise, there is no good to those who have forgetfulness.
translation: Just as there is no fortress that can protect those who are fearful, there is no good that can come to those who are negligent.
modern: அச்சம் உடையவர்களுக்குப் பாதுகாப்புத் தரும் அரண் என்று எதுவும் இல்லை; அதுபோல, மறதியும் அலட்சியமும் உடையவர்களுக்கு எந்த நன்மையும் உண்டாவதில்லை.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful analogy to warn against negligence or forgetfulness (பொச்சாப்பு). A person who is constantly gripped by fear cannot find safety even within a mighty fortress, because their own mind defeats them. Similarly, a person who is careless and forgetful can never achieve any lasting good or success, regardless of their opportunities. The poet emphasizes that internal discipline and alertness are far more critical than external circumstances.
